svg.title: Routing a match to its month
svg.desc: An animation in five steps. An online game records its matches in a table partitioned by range on played_on, with one partition per month for January, February, and March 2026, and the parent table stores no rows itself. Match 51190, played on 14 February 2026, is looked up on a date line by its played_on date and stored in matches_2026_02. Match 51468, played on 1 March 2026, lands on the bound that February and March share. February's TO excludes that date and March's FROM includes it, so the match is stored in matches_2026_03. Match 52235, played on 9 April 2026, finds no partition and no default partition, so the insert fails with an error. Then matches_2026_04 is created for April, and the same match is inserted again and stored in it.
svg.text: Routing a match to its month
The partitioned table holds no rows. Each match goes to the partition whose range covers its played_on date.

g.text: matches (match_id, winner_id, map_id, played_on) PARTITION BY RANGE (played_on)
holds no rows of its own
ERROR: no partition of relation "matches" found for row
DETAIL: Partition key of the failing row contains (played_on) = (2026-04-09).
CREATE TABLE matches_2026_04 PARTITION OF matches

svg.text: The matches table is split into one partition per month. The parent stores no rows of its own; it only routes them.
A match played on 14 February falls inside February's range, so it goes to matches_2026_02.
A match played on 1 March goes to March, because a range includes its lower bound (FROM) and excludes its upper bound (TO).
No partition covers 9 April and there is no DEFAULT partition to take the row, so the insert fails.
So create next month's partition ahead of time. With matches_2026_04 in place, the same match lands in April.
